reader_question: Where do the states with the most renter households sit on rent and renters’ income?
title: The four states with the most renter households held 17.1 million of the nation’s 46.6 million in 2025, and three of them had median rents above the nation’s.
measure_line: Median gross rent a month against renter households’ median income a year, 2025, 50 states and DC; each circle is a state, its area set by its renter households.
reading_guide: States to the right have renters with higher incomes, and states higher up have higher rents. A larger circle holds more renter households; the four largest are named.
notes: The cloud shows rent and income moving together across the states; it does not show one causes the other.

California’s median rent of $2,160 a month, New York’s $1,704 and Florida’s $1,866 sit above the nation’s $1,557, and Texas’s $1,515 below it, each by more than the gap’s margin of error. Margins of error are at 90 percent confidence.
alt: A bubble chart of 50 states and DC: median gross rent against renter households’ median income in 2025, each circle sized by renter households. The circles climb from lower left to upper right. The four largest, California with 6.2 million renter households, Texas with 4.3 million, New York with 3.6 million and Florida with 3.0 million, are named in the text’s ink; three sit above the nation’s rent and Texas below it.

table.caption: Rent, renter income and renter households by state, 2025

columns.label: Rent as a percent of income

chart_notes: The four states with the most renter households take the text’s ink, each named with its renter households; the other states are gray circles with thin outlines. The open ring marks the United States. The key gives circles for 1 million and 6 million renter households.

labels.x_axis: Renter households’ median income, a year
